cards.proof_strategy: Identify coordinate projection as a continuous linear functional.
sketch_steps: Identify coordinate projection as a continuous linear functional.
Use the standard product norm on the finite coordinate space.
The derivative of this projection is the projection itself at every point.
Retain arbitrary n and the valid coordinate index i in the conclusion.

cards.proof_strategy: Obtain a nonzero pair of weak Lagrange multipliers.

Thus divide by the objective multiplier and set λ=−a/b.
Evaluate the functional equality on arbitrary vectors to obtain B=λA.

cards.proof_strategy: Keep the entire finite family of level-set constraints.

Apply finite-family Lagrange multipliers to their derivative functionals.
The multiplier vector and objective multiplier are jointly nonzero, without claiming either one individually is nonzero.

cards.canonical_statement: For all coordinate dimensions m,n with chosen coordinates i,j and every nonzero real a, define f(x,y)=0 when xᵢ=0 or yⱼ=0, and a otherwise. Both block partial derivatives at the origin exist and are zero, yet f is not continuous there. Thus isolated partial derivatives cannot establish total differentiability.
cards.proof_strategy: On each block axis the other selected coordinate is zero, so the restricted function is identically zero.
sketch_steps: On each block axis the other selected coordinate is zero, so the restricted function is identically zero.
Both block derivatives therefore exist and are zero.
If the full function were continuous, values sufficiently close to the origin would have absolute value below |a|/2.
Choose both coordinate blocks equal to a small nonzero constant vector: the point is arbitrarily close, but the function value is a, contradicting the bound.
